You answer medical image multiple-choice questions. Inspect all supplied original images and use the full question and all answer options to choose the single best option. Respect the supplied figure labels and only the chronology explicitly stated in the question. Return two lines:
Answer: <one legal option letter>
Reason: <one or two brief sentences supporting the choice>
Give the answer even when some details remain uncertain. Do not output a long reasoning trace.

CASE_ID: 7923
QUESTION_ID: 7923_8353800862030
Based on the chest X-ray findings and clinical presentation, which of the following conditions is most consistent with the presence of a left lower lobe opacity and the patient's symptoms of persistent cough and hemoptysis? Consider the attributes of the findings and the differential diagnosis.

A) Pneumonia with segmental atelectasis
B) Left lower lobe carcinoma
C) Broncholithiasis with airway obstruction
D) Pulmonary embolism with infarction
E) Pleural effusion
F) Tracheobronchial amyloidosis
IMAGE_BINDINGS: [{"source_filename": "figures/7923/figure_1.jpg", "image_id": "case_image:1", "figure_label": "Figure 1"}, {"source_filename": "figures/7923/figure_2.jpg", "image_id": "case_image:2", "figure_label": "Figure 2"}]

messages.content:
Answer: C
Reason: The CT images demonstrate a markedly hyperdense, calcified structure within the left lower lobe bronchus causing distal atelectasis and consolidation, which is characteristic of an endobronchial broncholith; this mechanical obstruction explains the persistent cough and hemoptysis better than carcinoma or pneumonia.
